To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

many neurons in both sensory trigeminal nuclear complexes are bilaterally innervated by afferent fibers from the canine teeth and that this bilateral projection crosses the midline within the brain stem.

(a) the canine dental pulpal projection to the cat sensory trigeminus is predominantly unilateral; (b) the contralateral projection crosses in the medulla and pons, and not at the midbrain level, and (c) the ipsilateral projection is not interrupted by a central decussation.

the sensory trigeminal neurons of cats are innervated bilaterally by the canine dental pulpal nerves and that the projection from each contralateral pulp is composed exclusively of primary and higher afferent fibers.

the neuroanatomy of the trigeminal sensory system.

the organization of afferent projections to the trigeminal nuclei from the canine tooth pulp and with the effects upon this projection of unilateral transection of the trigeminal ganglia and of unilateral electrical stimulation of the canine teeth.
the neurophysiological basis for the phenomenon of referred pain and the role of the trigeminal system in this process.

the canine dental pulpal projections to neurons of the sensory trigeminal nuclear complex in cats is a bilateral phenomenon.
